title: Philosophy’s recurring mistakes—and the ideas worth rescuing

nodes.label: Anaximander
nodes.claim: Reality exceeds every named element; worlds emerge from an indefinite source.
nodes.opinion: A productive refusal to confuse a favored ingredient with reality itself.

nodes.label: Heraclitus
nodes.claim: Reality is patterned change; identity persists through tension.
nodes.opinion: Still fresher than most substance metaphysics. The slogan “everything flows” is crude, but process is the right default.

nodes.label: Parmenides
nodes.claim: What truly is cannot become what it is not.
nodes.opinion: A brilliant logical trap that turns grammar into ontology. Useful as a stress test, disastrous as a world picture.

nodes.label: Democritus
nodes.claim: Complex appearances arise from atoms and void.
nodes.opinion: The reductionist wager pays enormous scientific dividends, but experience is not explained merely by shrinking the furniture.

nodes.label: Plato
nodes.claim: Stable intelligible Forms are more real than changing appearances.
nodes.opinion: An immortal machine for asking normative questions—and a seductive source of anti-body, anti-change metaphysics. Fame is not a truth warrant.

nodes.label: Aristotle
nodes.claim: Form is embodied organization, not a second world.
nodes.opinion: Usually the better ancient guide to living form, though his hierarchy of nature aged badly.

nodes.label: Descartes
nodes.claim: Thinking substance and extended substance are fundamentally different.
nodes.opinion: A first-rate problem statement attached to a terrible solution. The split still haunts neuroscience disguised as “representation.”

nodes.label: Spinoza
nodes.claim: Mind and body are two attributes of one immanent reality.
nodes.opinion: The map’s backbone: the cleanest early escape from the Cartesian trap, though geometric certainty is more performance than proof.

nodes.label: Leibniz
nodes.claim: Reality consists of perspective-bearing monads coordinated without causal exchange.
nodes.opinion: A dazzling anticipation of distributed perspective; the pre-established harmony is metaphysical duct tape.

nodes.label: Berkeley
nodes.claim: To exist is to be perceived or to perceive.
nodes.opinion: Coherent enough to embarrass naive realism; gains little by relabeling the whole universe “mind.”

nodes.label: Hume
nodes.claim: The self and causality are habits assembled from impressions.
nodes.opinion: Excellent acid for bad metaphysics. Less good at explaining why stable practices survive his acid bath.

nodes.label: Kant
nodes.claim: Experience is structured by conditions supplied by cognition; things-in-themselves remain beyond direct knowledge.
nodes.opinion: The necessary checkpoint against naive access to reality. His cure risks turning the mind into a new prison.

nodes.label: Hegel
nodes.claim: Concepts and social forms develop through contradictions toward fuller self-comprehension.
nodes.opinion: Feedback, mediation, and historical intelligibility: keep. Totalizing closure and providential tone: cut. “End of history” is mostly his afterlife.

nodes.label: Schopenhauer
nodes.claim: Representation is driven by blind striving or Will.
nodes.opinion: Piercing about appetite and suffering; his cosmic pessimism overfits a temperament into an ontology.

nodes.label: Kierkegaard
nodes.claim: Truth that matters is lived through commitment, anxiety, and singular choice.
nodes.opinion: A needed antidote to Hegelian aerial photography; faith is not compulsory to keep the insight.

nodes.label: Baudelaire
nodes.claim: Modernity is transient, artificial, urban, intoxicating—and must be read aesthetically.
nodes.opinion: Not a system-builder, which is part of his value: a sensor for modern experience before theory embalms it.

nodes.label: Nietzsche
nodes.claim: Truths are embodied perspectives; values are made, contested, and sedimented.
nodes.opinion: The great de-moralizer of metaphysics. Perspectivism is disciplined interpretation, not permission for any claim whatsoever.

nodes.label: Bergson
nodes.claim: Lived duration is qualitative flow, not clock time cut into spatial units.
nodes.opinion: Indispensable for time and experience. Élan vital can be retired without losing duration or creative becoming.

nodes.label: Husserl
nodes.claim: Consciousness is intentional: always consciousness of something.
nodes.opinion: A precise return to experience, burdened by fantasies of presuppositionless method.

nodes.label: Freud
nodes.claim: The conscious ego is not master in its own house.
nodes.opinion: The unconscious remains essential; many hydraulic details and clinical universalizations do not.

nodes.label: Early Wittgenstein
nodes.claim: A proposition pictures a possible fact; what cannot be said should be passed over.
nodes.opinion: A beautiful attempt to fence nonsense that accidentally reveals how much life occurs outside the fence.

nodes.label: Logical positivism
nodes.claim: Meaningful claims are empirically verifiable or analytically true.
nodes.opinion: Excellent intellectual hygiene; verificationism fails its own test and amputates ethics, aesthetics, history, and much of science.

nodes.label: Heidegger
nodes.claim: Human existence is already involved in a meaningful world before detached cognition.
nodes.opinion: Deep correction to spectator theories of mind; needless obscurity and catastrophic politics demand permanent warning labels.

nodes.label: Aldous Huxley
nodes.claim: Ordinary consciousness may filter a wider field of experience; altered states can disclose neglected modes.
nodes.opinion: Take the phenomenology seriously. Treat the perennial philosophy as comparative poetry, not a culturally neutral discovery.

nodes.label: Kojève
nodes.claim: Hegel’s struggle for recognition culminates in a post-historical order.
nodes.opinion: Electrifying interpretation, weak prophecy. History changes costume; it does not clock out.

nodes.label: Sartre
nodes.claim: Consciousness is freedom and negation, condemned to choose.
nodes.opinion: Bad faith remains sharp. Radical freedom underestimates embodiment, trauma, institutions, and luck.

nodes.label: Camus
nodes.claim: The world offers no final answer; revolt creates dignity without metaphysical consolation.
nodes.opinion: More honest than systems promising closure: lucid limits, solidarity, and no cosmic receipt.

nodes.label: Merleau-Ponty
nodes.claim: Perception is enacted by a lived body already intertwined with the world.
nodes.opinion: One of the strongest bridges from phenomenology to contemporary embodied cognition.

nodes.label: Saussure
nodes.claim: Signs acquire meaning through differences within a system.
nodes.opinion: Foundational and powerful—so long as the system does not swallow bodies, history, and material practice.

nodes.label: Later Wittgenstein
nodes.claim: Meaning is use within forms of life; many philosophical knots are misuse of language.
nodes.opinion: One of philosophy’s best anti-philosophies. Therapy beats grand theory surprisingly often.

nodes.label: Lacan
nodes.claim: The subject is split by language; desire circles what symbolization cannot supply.
nodes.opinion: A potent diagram of desire and misrecognition, surrounded by cultic obscurity and thin empirical constraint.

nodes.label: Dennett
nodes.claim: There is no Cartesian theater; multiple distributed processes compete and revise.
nodes.opinion: The demolition is right. The leap from “no inner screen” to “phenomenality is explained or illusory” is not. Location is dependence, not explanation.

nodes.label: Nagel
nodes.claim: Objective descriptions omit what experience is like for the subject.
nodes.opinion: Still the cleanest reminder that third-person completeness has not been demonstrated.

nodes.label: Foucault
nodes.claim: Knowledge and subjectivity are formed inside practices of power.
nodes.opinion: Essential correction to disembodied epistemology. Genealogy diagnoses better than it governs.

nodes.label: Deleuze & Guattari
nodes.claim: Reality is productive difference, multiplicity, assemblage, and rhizomatic becoming.
nodes.opinion: The best cartography for process after Spinoza and Nietzsche—also a machine that can manufacture empty jargon.

nodes.label: Derrida
nodes.claim: Meaning depends on differences and deferrals that prevent final self-presence.
nodes.opinion: A durable tool against binary certainty. Deconstruction is close reading, not a license for mush.

nodes.label: Baudrillard
nodes.claim: Signs and models can precede and organize what counts as reality.
nodes.opinion: Prophetic about media saturation; “everything is simulation” becomes the totalizing gesture it mocks.

nodes.label: Chalmers
nodes.claim: Functional explanation leaves the hard problem: why is processing accompanied by experience?
nodes.opinion: Correctly preserves the explanandum. Conceivability arguments do not automatically settle ontology.

nodes.label: Žižek
nodes.claim: Ideology persists in practices and enjoyment even when belief becomes cynical.
nodes.opinion: A gifted contradiction detector and philosophical clown; signal diluted by compulsive repetition and performance.

nodes.label: 4E cognition
nodes.claim: Mind is embodied, embedded, enacted, and sometimes extended through organism–world coupling.
nodes.opinion: The most promising broad correction to brain-in-a-vat cognitive science; extension claims still require careful boundaries.

nodes.label: Panpsychism / Russellian monism
nodes.claim: Experience or proto-experience is fundamental rather than produced from wholly non-experiential matter.
nodes.opinion: Avoids brute emergence, inherits the combination problem. Best treated as a live metaphysical hypothesis, not a discovery.

nodes.label: Global neuronal workspace
nodes.claim: A representation becomes consciously accessible when globally broadcast through recurrent brain networks.
nodes.opinion: Strong on access, report, and flexible control; may explain availability better than felt presence.

nodes.label: Integrated information theory 4.0
nodes.claim: Consciousness corresponds to irreducible intrinsic cause–effect structure.
nodes.opinion: Bold and formal, but its metaphysical reach outruns current tests and yields counterintuitive assignments.

nodes.label: Higher-order theories
nodes.claim: A mental state becomes conscious when represented by a higher-order state.
nodes.opinion: Useful for metacognition; risks mistaking knowing that one sees for seeing.

nodes.label: Recurrent processing
nodes.claim: Local recurrent sensory processing may suffice for phenomenal consciousness before report.
nodes.opinion: A parsimonious rival to prefrontal-heavy access theories; boundaries remain contested.

nodes.label: Predictive processing
nodes.claim: Perception is hierarchical inference constrained by sensory prediction error.
nodes.opinion: A powerful account of perception and action, not by itself a complete theory of consciousness.

nodes.label: Active inference
nodes.claim: Organisms act to maintain viable states by minimizing expected surprise through perception and action.
nodes.opinion: Excellent organism-level framework; consciousness is often smuggled in rather than derived.

nodes.label: Beautiful Loop theory
nodes.claim: A hierarchically deep world-model becomes reflexively self-evidencing: it models a world that includes its own modeling existence.
nodes.opinion: One of the most interesting new active-inference proposals; conceptually fertile, empirically immature, and not yet a solution to felt experience.

nodes.label: Dendritic integration theory
nodes.claim: Apical dendrites may integrate context with feedforward content in ways crucial to conscious processing.
nodes.opinion: Promising bridge between cellular mechanism and large-scale theories; still not an answer to why mechanism feels.

nodes.label: Attention schema theory
nodes.claim: The brain models its own attention and reports that simplified model as awareness.
nodes.opinion: Explains self-modeling and report elegantly; the model may still leave experience standing outside the explanation.

nodes.label: Affective / brainstem accounts
nodes.claim: Valenced organismic feeling may be more basic than cortical report or cognition.
nodes.opinion: A necessary correction to vision-centric, cortex-centric theories; precise sufficiency claims remain open.

nodes.label: COGITATE adversarial test
nodes.claim: Preregistered tests found important predictions of both GNWT and IIT unsupported or complicated.
nodes.opinion: The healthiest result: no coronation. Consciousness science needs sharper discriminating predictions, not fan clubs.

nodes.label: Orch-OR
nodes.claim: Quantum state reductions in neuronal microtubules generate conscious moments.
nodes.opinion: Interesting only insofar as it produces risky, discriminating tests. Quantum vocabulary is not explanatory pixie dust.

nodes.label: Nassim Haramein
nodes.claim: Cosmic geometry and vacuum structure are invoked to connect matter, information, and consciousness.
nodes.opinion: Treat as speculative cosmological storytelling, not a credible consciousness theory, until independent testable evidence exists.
